study.title: Real-Time Coronary Artery Dominance Classification from Angiographic Images Using Advanced Deep Video Architectures

imaging.modality_detail: Invasive coronary angiography video sequences (RCA and LCA projections) from the public CoronaryDominance dataset
imaging.territory_detail: Coronary arteries (RCA and LCA); coronary dominance by origin of the posterior descending artery

public_dataset_used.detail: CoronaryDominance dataset (Kruzhilov et al., Sci. Data 2025), https://huggingface.co/datasets/BearSubj13/CoronaryDominance

data_released.detail: Data availability statement points to the existing public CoronaryDominance dataset; no new data released

task.task_description: Binary video-level classification of coronary artery dominance (right vs left) from whole angiographic video sequences without separating RCA and LCA projections, comparing TSN, Video Swin Transformer and VideoMAEv2 implemented in MMAction2.
task.clinical_application: Automated coronary dominance assessment for SYNTAX/Gensini scoring, risk stratification and revascularization planning; real-time decision support in the cath lab/PACS

temporal_evidence.quote: transformer architectures, including VideoMAEv2 and the Video Swin Transformer, utilize self-attention mechanisms that dynamically focus on spatially and temporally distributed regions of interest

method.pretraining: VideoMAEv2: ViT-G (Kinetics-710) self-supervised masked autoencoder weights; Video Swin: Swin-L (ImageNet22K); TSN: ResNet-50 (ImageNet)
method.class_imbalance_handling: No oversampling or synthetic balancing (deliberately); stratified splitting and class-sensitive metrics (recall, F1, MCC)

comparators: Kruzhilov et al. multi-stage RCA/LCA classification approach

G2.quote: The current models should be tested on extensive datasets obtained from diverse geographic regions, devices, and patient populations for prospective and multi-center clinical validation

G3.quote: The integrated approach processes entire angiographic video sequences, eliminating the need for separate RCA and LCA identification during preprocessing

G5.quote: This ability presents a substantial solution to the commonly encountered problem of limited labeled data in the healthcare domain

G6.quote: for prospective and multi-center clinical validation. This is crucial for verifying generalizability and reliability

G7.quote: lack of inherent interpretability remains a concern. The transparency of decision-making processes is critically important for clinical trust and acceptance

G8.quote: Diagnostic accuracy could be improved by integrating other modalities such as electrocardiogram (ECG), echocardiogram (ECHO), clinical notes, and laboratory data in addition to angiographic videos

G9.quote: Class imbalance presents a significant challenge, particularly affecting the training and validation processes for less represented classes such as left dominance

other_limitations: Performance below the multi-stage artery-specific method of Kruzhilov et al. on the same dataset
No RCA/LCA distinction, vessel segmentation or artery-focused preprocessing
No artifact or low-quality frame removal
Unified RCA-LCA data may lose anatomical specificity and mask specific arterial anomalies
k-fold cross-validation not performed due to computational cost
future_work: Explainability via attention maps and Grad-CAM
Prospective multi-center validation on diverse regions, devices and populations
Multimodal integration of ECG, echocardiography, clinical notes and laboratory data
Hybrid Video Swin Transformer and VideoMAEv2 models
Software integration into PACS/CCTA clinical workflow
